text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. Since you contacted me, I’m including A and B too. I can help facilitate a needs conversation; I can't make legal decisions or move money. I won't suggest outcomes yet.

I’ll keep one short "Current needs list" block, send the latest to all three whenever it changes, and not take silence as agreement. "NCE" means a brief, positive wording of what matters that the person says fits; I’ll check wording with each person before recording it.

For each concern you raised, please tell me what matters to you and why:
- About A/her husband buying at a "family discount" and your not signing off: what matters to you, and why?
- About B being able to use some money: what matters to you, and why?
- Anything else about the house, will, grief, timing, or sister relationship: what matters, and why?

If you may not yet trust that your needs matter, or you're holding back, say "slow down" and I’ll ask again before treating anything as settled. Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with this way of starting? A no or small discomfort is a need to add, not a problem to overcome.

Draft process options (v1 — for validation, not agreement; process protections, not final outcomes):
Common to A–C: no one speaks for another (including as twins or as the younger sister); C claims no authority over A or B; no sign-off, discount, sale, buyout, or money move is assumed; A’s and B’s hopes are considered, not dismissed or granted; C’s share/choices/time are respected; all get clear info and room for their own view; any later step needs each sister’s fresh voluntary yes.
A) Information-first pause. For now, no sign-off, sale, buyout, discount, or money move. A’s stable-home/independence hope, B’s studio/independence hope, and C’s share/consent boundary are recorded as live needs. Each sister may seek clear, independent legal/valuation/process info, ask questions, speak for herself, and take her own time. Any later step needs a fresh voluntary yes from each.
B) Separate advice + facilitated needs round. Each sister may consult her own adviser; then a no-negotiation conversation where each restates her NCE and questions, and a neutral professional gives general information to all three. If anyone later wants to explore a purchase or another arrangement, she can request a separate, consent-based discussion, with no pressure and no assumed discount or use of C’s share. No decision without info, time, and each sister’s clear yes.
C) Written check-in only. Share a short note that nothing about the house is agreed; each sister lists what info she needs and what would help her form her own view; set a revisit date only if all three want one. Anyone can say no, add a need, or slow down; nothing is settled until each says what fits.
